displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that a physical resurrection is a reasonable cumulative explanation when early bodily proclamation, identity continuity, reported encounters, transformative conduct, and the missing-body tradition are compared together rather than demanded to prove the event independently.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the live case by making its conclusion explicitly cumulative and comparative rather than treating any isolated consideration as decisive.

premises.text: Jewish resurrection expectations and Pauline transformed-body language make corporeal continuity more contextually natural than a reading limited to disembodied postmortem survival.

novelty.explanation: This develops the existing Pauline argument while preserving the acknowledged interpretive uncertainty.

premises.text: Eating, touching, retained wounds, and the empty-tomb tradition jointly portray continuity of personal identity and embodiment despite extraordinary transformed capacities.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the earlier underdeveloped reconciliation between bodily continuity and unusual postmortem capacities.

premises.text: The conversions of James and Paul and the reported transition to public proclamation are relevant as cumulative conduct evidence, although they establish sincere conviction more directly than physical resurrection.

novelty.explanation: This narrows the conduct evidence to its defensible force and avoids treating transformative sincerity as direct event verification.

premises.text: An adequate alternative should explain both the missing-body tradition and the encounter traditions while avoiding unnecessary mechanisms, but dependencies among natural mechanisms must be assessed rather than presumed.

novelty.explanation: This preserves the conjunction insight while correcting its insufficient treatment of dependence and comparative assumptions.

premises.text: Rival miracle traditions should be evaluated using the same criteria of source proximity, independence, incentives, background knowledge, physical specificity, and explanatory integration.

novelty.explanation: This turns scattered disanalogies into a stable comparative framework that includes the strongest skeptical parity objection.

conclusion.text: Taken cumulatively, these considerations can make physical resurrection a historically reasonable explanation for someone who permits supernatural causation, while leaving substantial uncertainty about source independence, bodily detail, and natural alternatives.

novelty.explanation: This supplies a proportionate conclusion that incorporates the principal evidential limitations exposed during the exchange.

newArguments.title: Comparative Explanatory Compression
newArguments.text: A stronger cumulative case would compare how many independently motivated assumptions each explanation requires across bodily proclamation, reported appearances, conversion, conduct, and the tomb tradition. Resurrection should not receive a free pass merely because it is a single label, but neither should several natural mechanisms be counted as one explanation without examining their coordination. The relevant question is comparative compression: which account explains the greatest range of data with the fewest unsupported auxiliary commitments, given each participant's background assumptions about supernatural possibility?

novelty.explanation: This introduces an explicit explanatory-compression framework not articulated as such in any locked participant move.

newArguments.title: Constraint from Early Claim Content
newArguments.text: The evidential significance of early proclamation depends not merely on its date but on its content. If the earliest recoverable claim already concerned the crucified Jesus's resurrection rather than generic heavenly vindication, later bodily narratives may elaborate an existing corporeal core instead of creating it wholesale. This argument requires careful linguistic and source analysis and does not establish every Gospel detail, but it gives the affirmative case a principled way to resist a simple progression from vision to physicality while acknowledging development in narrative presentation.

novelty.explanation: This develops the early-proclamation point into a direct answer to the strongest source-development challenge.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that the surviving evidence supports early sincere resurrection belief but does not specifically warrant a physical resurrection when bodily descriptions, witness independence, corroboration, and natural alternatives remain materially uncertain.

novelty.explanation: This consolidates the skeptical case while expressly conceding sincere early belief and avoiding a stronger historical denial.

premises.text: Pauline terminology and later Gospel descriptions do not provide one uncontested evidential standard for ordinary physical embodiment, especially where touching and eating coexist with extraordinary capacities.

novelty.explanation: This combines the ambiguity and development arguments into one qualified source-critical premise.

premises.text: Paul's report of five hundred witnesses lacks surviving identities, circumstances, independence checks, and direct testimony, limiting its value as externally verifiable group corroboration.

novelty.explanation: This develops the corroboration deficit without inferring that the reported gathering therefore never occurred.

premises.text: Conversions, costly proclamation, persecution, and martyrdom principally establish conviction unless identifiable witnesses can be linked to firsthand bodily encounters and consequences specifically imposed for maintaining that testimony.

novelty.explanation: This strengthens the knowledge-to-cost distinction that carried the skeptical sincerity analysis.

premises.text: Reburial, theft, visionary experience, memory development, and narrative elaboration remain candidate mechanisms whose comparative plausibility requires integration rather than mere enumeration.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the natural-alternative case by accepting the affirmative demand for an integrated explanation.

premises.text: Mormon and other rival traditions require consistent evaluation of estrangement, incentives, physical specificity, source access, and background constraints without assuming either parity or decisive disanalogy in advance.

novelty.explanation: This preserves the parity test while incorporating the affirmative side's strongest proposed differences.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, the evidence can reasonably support early transformative resurrection conviction while remaining insufficiently specific to distinguish a physical resurrection from combinations of visionary, developmental, and burial-related explanations.

novelty.explanation: This states a bounded insufficiency conclusion rather than claiming that a physical resurrection has been historically disproved.

newArguments.title: Evidence-Type Separation
newArguments.text: A disciplined skeptical account should separate evidence into claim formation, witness sincerity, bodily specificity, and corpse location. Early proclamation may strongly support early belief; conversion and danger may support sincerity; Gospel scenes may support later bodily interpretation; and tomb traditions may support some missing-body claim. None of those evidential categories automatically transfers its strength to the others. This separation prevents a cumulative argument from gaining apparent force through repeated counting of dependent traditions and clarifies exactly where additional independent evidence would be needed.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a four-category evidence model not expressly formulated in the participant moves.

newArguments.title: Expected Corroboration Calibration
newArguments.text: The absence of independent postmortem corroboration matters only relative to what the historical circumstances make reasonable to expect. A stronger skeptical case would identify which alleged appearances were public enough, socially consequential enough, or connected to accessible witnesses strongly enough that additional testimony or hostile engagement might plausibly survive. This avoids treating ancient documentary silence as automatically decisive while still distinguishing a named report from independently recoverable witness evidence. The method strengthens the corroboration objection through calibrated expectations rather than a categorical appeal to missing records.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the compressed treatment of documentary silence by supplying an explicit expectation-sensitive standard.
